changes_made.explanation: Minor normalization of dataset name (CNN/DailyMail) and capitalization of output descriptions

Changed answer from No to Yes - the paper uses classification accuracy as an automatic evaluation metric to measure how well classifiers can distinguish between different model configurations based on generated text artifacts
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper
The paper mentions concurrent work investigating human raters but does not conduct its own human evaluations

overall_notes: Paper focuses on detecting artifacts in NLG outputs rather than traditional NLG evaluation. The main evaluation is classification accuracy for distinguishing model configurations. While several models are mentioned (GPT, GPT-2, CTRL, Grover), only Grover was actually used for generation in their experiments. The paper establishes that NLG model choices leave detectable signatures in generated text.
